Photo receptors: These receptors are found only in the dorsal surface and more abundant in prostomium and peristomium. They are absent in clitellum. Such receptors help the animal to judge intensity of light falling on the body. 8.3.7 REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEM Reproduction is the life process in which living beings produce offspring of their own kinds for the continuation of their generation. Earthworm is a hermaphrodite (monoecious) animal bearing both male and female reproductive organs in the same body. But self-fertilization doesn’t occur because they are protandrous animal. Protandry is the condition where male reproductive organs mature earlier than the female reproductive organs. So, cross fertilization takes place by the process of copulation between two sexually mature worms which is followed by cocoon formation.

Activity 8.9 Observe the reproductive system of earthworm. Objective: To identify the different reproductive organs of earthworm Materials required: Dissecting tray, forceps, needle, and blade Procedure: i. Take a preserved earthworm ii. Pin down it on the tray by dorsal surface facing upwards iii. Make a longitudinal incision in the mid-dorsal line from 25th segment up to the anterior end. iv. Release the flaps of body wall from the septa with needles and pin down them v. Identify the reproductive organs and note the segments in which they lie. (Take help of your teacher) vi. Figure 8.3.19 Reproductive system of earthworm A. Male reproductive organs: 1. Testes There are two pairs of very minute, white and lobed structures called testes. Each pair of testes is present in the 10th and 11th segment. Each testis lies ventro-laterally on the either side of ventral nerve cord. They are attached to the anterior wall of respective testis sacs. Each testis consists of a narrow compact base from which arises 4-8 finger like processes containing round ball of cells called spermatogonia. Spermatogonia shed off into the testis sac and passed into seminal vesicles for maturation i.e. to transform into spermatozoa. 2. Testis sacs Testis sacs are wide, white and thin-walled and fluid filled sacs which enclose testes in 10th and 11th segment. They are situated ventro-laterally below the alimentary canal. Each testis sac also encloses a pair of ciliated spermiducal funnels. Testis sac of 11th segment is larger. Testis sacs communicate with seminal vesicles by narrow ducts. 3. Seminal vesicles There are two pairs of white coloured large sac like structures, each pair lying in 11th and 12th segment called as seminal vesicles. Seminal vesicles of 12th segments are comparatively larger and not enclosed within testis sac. Seminal vesicles are developed as outgrowth of septum and hence called septal pouches. Seminal vesicles of 11th segment communicate with testis sac of 10th segment and seminal vesicles of 12th segment communicate with testis sac of 11th segment. 4. Spermiducal funnel/spermatic funnel Spermiducal funnels are two pair of cup like structures and having ciliated and folded margin.
